gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histologically diagnosed glioblastoma patients who have been confirmed the progression of disease after attempting standard therapy

candidate_evidence.quote: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of GX-I7 in combination with bevacizumab in subjects with recurrent glioblastoma.

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: Absolute counts and ratios of immune cell subtypes: Changes of absolute counts and ratios of immune cell subtypes

role_evidence.quote: Bevacizumab at a dose of 10 mg/kg intravenously, and GX-I7 intramuscularly.
GX-I7 in Combination With Bevacizumab in Recurrent Glioblastoma (GBM) Patients

agents.drug_class_hint: long-acting recombinant human interleukin-7 Fc fusion protein (rhIL-7-hyFc), immune agonist

role_evidence.quote: Bevacizumab at a dose of 10 mg/kg intravenously, and GX-I7 intramuscularly.
Subjects who have received bevacizumab or other VEGF inhibitors prior to study participation

agents.drug_class_hint: anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody; established GBM therapy

coder_notes: Single-arm GX-I7 (efineptakin alfa, INN given in record) plus bevacizumab at a standard 10 mg/kg dose; bevacizumab is an established GBM therapy given in the only arm and not itself the question, so coded soc_backbone. Target engagement coded yes on the planned change in blood immune-cell subset counts (IL-7 pharmacodynamic effect); ADA endpoints are immunogenicity, not target engagement.
